mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during GDP growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative when UNRATE is below 5% in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP and payroll employment indicates strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between GDP and payroll growth with SPX returns over a 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production suggests higher economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between industrial production growth and SPX returns over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real estate investment signifies strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not positive when RSAFS growth exceeds 5% in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation combined with low unemployment leads to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No negative correlation between high inflation/low unemployment and SPX returns over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment in a late-cycle expansion indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not positive when UNRATE is below 5% in more than 50% of late-cycle cases.
